title: Tile and grout sealing
audience: Tilers and tile-care workers who seal tile and grout on floors and walls
learningOutcomes: Select a sealer suited to the tile, the grout and the exposure, using the data sheet.
Clean and dry the tile and grout before sealing, and test the sealer on a small area.
Explain the boundary between sealing and waterproofing, and refer waterproofing work.

instruction.heading: Sealing is not waterproofing
instruction.body: A sealer protects porous tile and grout from stains and dirt. It does not make a wet area waterproof, and it does not repair a failed membrane or a cracked grout line. Natural stone, unglazed tile and cementitious grout are the usual candidates for sealing, and glazed tile normally needs grout sealing only. Confirm the tile and grout type before choosing a sealer, because some sealers change the look of the surface or are not compatible with some stone. Waterproofing is referred under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”.

instruction.heading: Clean, test and apply
instruction.body: Clean the tile and grout fully before sealing, because any residue is sealed in. Let the surface dry for the time the data sheet requires, and check the moisture before sealing. Test the sealer on a small hidden area and check the appearance after it dries. Apply the sealer in thin, even coats, and do not flood the surface. Wipe off excess before it dries, and keep traffic off the surface until the data sheet's cure time has passed. Record the product, the batch, the coats and the cure time.

procedure: Identify the tile and grout type and check the sealer's data sheet for compatibility.
Clean the tile and grout fully, and rinse off all residue.
Dry the surface and check the moisture to the data sheet requirement.
Test the sealer on a small hidden area and check the appearance after drying.
Apply the sealer in thin, even coats and wipe off the excess before it dries.
Keep traffic off the surface for the cure time and record the product, batch, coats and cure time.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks you to seal a shower floor and says the grout lines have been leaking water onto the bathroom floor below.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the grout be sealed to stop the leak?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Sealing is not waterproofing, and a leak through the floor is a waterproofing or structural matter. Refer the leak under “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary” for assessment. Sealing the grout may be considered later as a separate task, after the leak source is confirmed and resolved.

equipmentAndPpe: Sealer per data sheet, with safety data sheet

commonErrors.error: Sealing over a leak and calling it waterproofed.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the leak. Sealing is not waterproofing.

commonErrors.error: Sealing without cleaning, so residue is trapped under the sealer.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean and rinse fully, and dry before sealing.

commonErrors.error: Applying a thick coat that pools and marks the surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply thin even coats and wipe off the excess before it dries.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Sealer products carry hazards on their safety data sheet. Read the SDS before use and follow the ventilation and protection it specifies.
Waterproofing: Queensland's QBCC classes name waterproofing for tiling and for plastering drywall (QBCC pages last reviewed 31 August 2021).
Completing this lesson does not give a tiling, waterproofing or building licence, and does not make a wet area waterproof.

qualityStandard: The sealer is chosen from the data sheet for the tile and grout type.
The surface is clean, dry and tested before the full area is sealed.
Leaks are referred and not treated as sealing work.
documentationEvidence: Sealing record with product, batch, coats, drying and cure times
Test area record with the appearance check
Referral note for any leak or waterproofing concern
summary: Sealing protects porous tile and grout; it does not waterproof a wet area.
Clean, dry and test before sealing, and apply thin even coats.

knowledgeChecks.question: A shower floor is leaking into the room below. A client asks for the grout to be sealed. What is correct?
options: Seal the grout and call it waterproofed, since the grout is the weak point
Paint the ceiling below the leak and say nothing to the client today
Seal the tile only, since the grout is fine as it is now and the floor is dry
Refer the leak under the waterproofing check, because sealing is not waterproofing

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must tile and grout be cleaned fully before sealing?
options: So residue is not sealed in under the sealer
So the sealer changes the colour of the tile
Because sealers do not bond to clean surfaces
It is not required on any tile at all today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which surfaces does the lesson name as the usual candidates for sealing?
options: Natural stone, unglazed tile and cementitious grout
